title: Every nested pattern likely has a formula in generalized hypergeometric functions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Every nested pattern likely has a formula in generalized hypergeometric functions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although most nested patterns have no obvious relation to ordinary mathematical functions, a formula for the color of each cell of any nested pattern can probably be found in terms of suitably generalized hypergeometric functions or similar generalizations of traditional functions.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 10: Processes of Perception and Analysis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it is my guess that in the end it will in fact turn out to be possible to get a formula for any nested pattern in terms of suitably generalized hypergeometric functions

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 10, “Processes of Perception and Analysis”; section “Traditional Mathematics and Mathematical Formulas” (from p. 606), p. 612. Scope: nested patterns generated by substitution systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch10-17: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.40

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Restricted representation theorems could be proved or disproved, but the phrase 'or similar generalizations' removes a stable refutation criterion. As stated, the conjecture cannot be resolved by computation or observation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A proof would require a fixed formal class of nested patterns and a fixed syntax for 'suitably generalized hypergeometric functions'; allowing unspecified similar generalizations makes every failed representation compatible with the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The permitted function class is open-ended.

Any nested pattern is already describable by its generating substitution program.

Finite successful examples cannot establish the universal quantifier.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Particular nested patterns, such as those tied to binomial coefficients modulo 2, have known formulas, and the hypergeometric class is a published, checkable target. The claim says any nested pattern, in functions that may be generalized as needed. Specific successes therefore test only a restricted scope, and the elastic generalization blocks a clean refutation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For substitution systems that generate nested patterns, search for a formula for each cell in a stated class of generalized hypergeometric functions. A uniform translation of every nested pattern into a fixed class would confirm the claim; escape into an ever-wider class of 'similar generalizations' leaves it unrefuted.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Suitably generalized' can be expanded until almost any nested formula counts.

Known closed forms for particular nested patterns do not yield a theorem for every substitution system.
